compatibility.title: Which Mitsubishi Models Use the 4N15?
compatibility.intro: The 4N15 was introduced in 2015 as Mitsubishi's modern 2.4‑litre diesel, replacing the older 4D56 2.5‑litre unit. It powers the L200/Triton pickup range and the Pajero Sport (Shogun Sport in the UK) SUV, with two power tunes available.

costGuide.title: Mitsubishi 4N15 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 4N15 typically takes 10-14 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent Mitsubishi specialist) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: The 4N15 is a complex modern diesel with a thin‑bore cylinder head that requires specialist care during injector removal. Prices vary based on whether the DPF and EGR system has been cleaned or replaced, whether the timing chain has been inspected, and whether the engine is a 154 hp or 181 hp variant. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide for context.

failures.title: Mitsubishi 4N15 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: DPF clogging and EGR carbon buildup
items.whatHappens: The 4N15's diesel particulate filter (DPF) and EGR valve are prone to rapid clogging, particularly on vehicles used for short urban trips where the DPF never reaches regeneration temperature. Symptoms include loss of power, reduced fuel efficiency, DPF warning lights, and limp mode. Poor fuel quality accelerates the problem.
items.repairVsReplace: DPF cleaning (around £300-£600) is usually the first step; if the DPF is damaged, replacement costs £800-£1,500. EGR valve cleaning (around £200-£400) is also effective. This is a maintenance issue, not a reason to replace the engine - but if left unaddressed, it can lead to turbo or engine damage. Read our full DPF failure guide

items.title: Piezo injector failure
items.whatHappens: The 4N15 uses sensitive piezo injectors that can fail prematurely, particularly with poor‑quality fuel. Symptoms include rough idle, excessive smoke, poor starting, and increased fuel consumption.
items.repairVsReplace: Injectors can be refurbished (around £150-£300 each) or replaced (around £300-£500 each). The 4N15's cylinder head has thin injector bores that can crack if injectors are removed carelessly or copper washers aren't renewed. Always use a specialist for this work.

items.title: Timing chain wear
items.whatHappens: The 4N15 uses a timing chain rather than a belt - it should last the life of the vehicle with proper maintenance. However, some owners have reported chain stretch or wear beyond 100,000 miles, particularly if the wrong oil has been used. The chain coordinates with the MIVEC variable valve timing system.
items.repairVsReplace: Timing chain replacement (around £800-£1,500) is the standard fix. Use the correct low‑SAPS oil (5W‑30, API CJ‑4 or equivalent) to protect the chain and DPF.

items.title: Intake manifold flap clogging
items.whatHappens: The intake manifold flaps accumulate soot and carbon deposits, causing them to stick and triggering engine control errors.
items.repairVsReplace: Manifold cleaning (around £300-£600) is usually sufficient; if the flaps are damaged, replacement may be required.

failures.goodYearsLine: The 4N15 is a fundamentally tough engine with no critical design flaws across its production run. Later versions (post‑2018) have improved timing chain longevity. The engine is known for its durability in demanding conditions and can exceed 300,000 km with proper maintenance.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 4N15
variants.intro: The 4N15 is a specific engine code within the Mitsubishi 4N family of diesel engines. Unlike some engines that fragment into many sub‑codes, the 4N15's variants are primarily distinguished by power output and application. 4N Family Overview: The 4N family includes: - 4N13 - 1.8L diesel, fitted to smaller models - 4N14 - 2.2L diesel, fitted to ASX and Outlander - 4N15 - 2.4L diesel, fitted to L200/Triton and Pajero Sport (this page) - 4N16 - 2.4L diesel, a later variant of the 4N15 Within the 4N15, the key distinctions are: - Standard‑power variant - 154 hp (113 kW) @ 3,500 rpm; 380 Nm torque; fitted to entry‑level L200 and Pajero Sport models - High‑power variant - 181 hp (133 kW) @ 3,500 rpm; 430 Nm torque; fitted to higher‑spec models - Market‑specific tuning - Some markets received different emissions calibration (Euro 5 compliance) The engine features an all‑aluminium block, DOHC 16‑valve cylinder head, common‑rail fuel system, variable‑geometry turbocharger (VGT), and MIVEC phase regulation. How to confirm your code: 1. On the engine - the 4N15 code is stamped on the engine block. Look for "4N15" on the identification plate on the front or side of the engine. 2. On the V5C logbook - the engine number is listed; cross‑reference with Mitsubishi parts systems. 3. VIN decode - use a Mitsubishi VIN decoder; the engine type will be shown. 4. Registration lookup - enter your reg above and we'll confirm the exact fitment. Similar‑looking codes it is commonly confused with: - Mitsubishi 4N14 - the 2.2‑litre version, fitted to ASX and Outlander; shares architecture but smaller displacement - Mitsubishi 4D56 - the 2.5‑litre predecessor; different block material and older design

relatives.description: 4D56 (2.5L Di‑D): - the 2.5-litre diesel that preceded the 4N15 in the L200 and Shogun Sport from 1996 to 2015. The 4D56 used an iron block compared to the 4N15's aluminium construction, and produced lower power (133-176 hp). The 4N15 brought MIVEC variable valve timing, higher injection pressure, and improved emissions compliance.

relatives.code: 4N16 (2.4L Di‑D): A later evolution of the 4N15, fitted to post
relatives.description: 2019 L200 and Shogun Sport models. It features revised emissions calibration and improved DPF regeneration strategies.

variants.closing: Why fitting the wrong revision matters: The 4N15 standard‑power and high‑power variants have different ECU calibration, turbocharger specification, and in some cases different injectors. A high‑power 181 hp engine can be fitted to a lower‑spec vehicle with appropriate ECU programming, but a lower‑power engine in a high‑spec vehicle will feel underpowered and may have compatibility issues. The 4N14 and 4D56 are not direct swaps.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 4N15 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used 4N15 makes sense for lower‑value L200 or Shogun Sport examples where the vehicle itself is worth under £8,000-£10,000. The key requirement is documented service history with the correct low‑SAPS 5W‑30 oil, and evidence that the DPF and EGR have been maintained. The primary risk with used units is undisclosed DPF clogging or injector wear - insist on a diagnostic scan, DPF pressure test, and injector balance check before purchase. Used units typically cost £2,000-£3,500. View used engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A proper 4N15 recon includes DPF professional cleaning or replacement, EGR valve cleaning or replacement, injector refurbishment or replacement, timing chain inspection, new gaskets and seals, and full service with correct oil. The cylinder head's thin injector bores require specialist care during rebuild. This is the right call for most replacements - you get a like‑new unit with the known weak points already addressed, backed by 12-24 months warranty. Reconditioned units typically cost £3,500-£5,000. View reconditioned engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full rebuild is justified for high‑value, low‑mileage or commercial‑use vehicles where the engine has suffered catastrophic failure (e.g. injector bore damage, timing chain failure). An upgraded rebuild should include new pistons, rings, bearings, timing chain kit, and a full set of gaskets. For standard applications, reconditioned is usually more cost‑effective. View rebuilt engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All engines can be supplied and fitted through our network of vetted UK Mitsubishi specialists - nationwide coverage with 12‑month warranty on labour and parts. View supply & fit
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: ** The 4N15 sits in commercial and SUV vehicles - Mitsubishi L200 (£8,000-£25,000), Mitsubishi Shogun Sport (£10,000-£30,000). A £3,500-£5,000 reconditioned engine plus £1,200-£1,500 fitting is a significant but often justifiable investment - typically 20-40% of the vehicle's value. For lower‑value commercial examples (sub‑£10,000 L200), a used engine with documented DPF and injector history may be more economic. For well‑maintained, high‑spec examples used for towing or off‑roading, the investment is usually justified given the vehicle's remaining capability. Always evaluate the whole‑vehicle condition, including chassis and bodywork, before committing.

items.question: What are the common problems with the Mitsubishi 4N15 engine?
items.answer: The 4N15's most common issues are DPF clogging and EGR carbon buildup (particularly with urban driving), piezo injector failure (often fuel-quality related), timing chain wear at high mileage, and intake manifold flap clogging. The engine is fundamentally tough but requires proper maintenance. DPF cleaning is essential for urban vehicles. Injector failure causes rough running and excessive smoke. Timing chain is generally robust but can stretch at 100,000+ miles.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 4N15 engine?
items.answer: A used 4N15 is only worth considering with documented service history using low-SAPS 5W-30 oil and evidence of DPF and EGR maintenance. A reconditioned unit is safer, including DPF cleaning, EGR cleaning, injector refurbishment and gaskets with 12-24 months warranty, typically costing £3,500-£5,000 supply-only. Used engines risk undisclosed DPF clogging and injector issues. Diagnostic scan and DPF pressure test are essential before purchase. Reconditioned units address known failure points.

items.question: Is the 4N15 a reliable engine?
items.answer: Yes - the 4N15 is considered a tough and durable diesel engine, capable of exceeding 300,000 km with proper maintenance. However, it requires regular DPF regeneration (motorway driving for urban vehicles), correct low-SAPS oil, and good fuel quality to avoid injector and DPF issues. DPF regeneration requires regular motorway driving. Use of low-SAPS 5W-30 oil is essential. Good fuel quality prevents injector wear.
